key_insight: The paper gives an end-to-end theory showing how finite data, network training, and numerical discretization together determine the final sampling quality of score-based diffusion models.
engineering_relevance: It provides practical guidance for choosing dataset size, time-step grids, and optimization accuracy to improve diffusion-model sample fidelity in real implementations.
method: Analyze score learning with practical ResNet-type parameterizations.
Derive a generalization/convergence framework from discrete finite-sample training to the ideal continuous-time objective.
Prove an end-to-end total variation error bound that splits generative error into truncation, reverse discretization, generalization, and optimization terms.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical total-variation-distance estimate, but does not mention empirical experiments or benchmark results.
watch_item: The bound depends on several coupled assumptions and error sources, so using it in practice requires careful control of discretization, optimization, and model capacity.
paper_title: From Score Learning to Discretized Sampling: An End-to-End Generalization Analysis of Diffusion Models
